AGENDA
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  SEPTEMBER 13, 2023

UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF ASSEMBLY
BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS PLANNING COMMISSION MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING: YOU
MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: planning@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING
BY CALLING 1-(669)-444-9171 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 929 283 6465 DURING THE MEETING
TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3
OR ON THE CITY’S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

  SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA TELECONFERENCE
  6:00 PM

  Rosa Barragan, Chair
  Linda Lopez, Vice Chair
  Kim Apodaca, Planning Commissioner
  Gabriel P. Garcia, Planning Commissioner
  Luis Navas, Planning Commissioner

 Public Comment:  Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: planning@norwalkca.gov, or through the
 video/teleconference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction subject to the rules of
 decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
 special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future
 Planning Commission meeting.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
 offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
 meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
 available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services
 are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
 posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection, by request in the Community Development Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk
 Boulevard during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday; telephone (562) 929-5744. You may also contact the City
 Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.
 CALL TO ORDER

FLAG SALUTE

Commissioner Navas

ROLL CALL OF MEMBERS

MINUTES

1.  MEETING MINUTES
  Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve the minutes of the Special Meeting of July 12,
  2023.

PUBLIC HEARING

2.  Precise Development Plan No. 2039 / Director Approval Request No. 5 / Variance No. 2022-01 to permit
  the construction of a new 2,393 square foot drive-through restaurant. Environmental: Consider and find
  the project exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15303 (New Construction of Small Structures) and
  Section 15332 (In-Fill Development Projects). The subject property is 12843 Norwalk Boulevard, located
  on the northwest corner of Norwalk Boulevard and Adoree Street.
  That the Planning Commission:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-19 to approve Precise Development Plan No. 2039 subject to the Conditions
  of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 23-20 to approve Director Approval Request No. 5 subject to the Conditions of
  Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 23-21 to approve Variance No. 2022-01 subject to the Conditions of Approval
  contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  4. Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15303 (New Construction of Small Structures) and Section 15332 (In-Fill
  Development Projects).

3.  General Plan Amendment No. 2022-03/ Zone Change No. 2022-05/ Tentative Parcel Map No. 2022-04 to
  permit the development of three (3) single-family homes on a 0.39-acre site. Environmental: Review and
  recommend adoption of the associated IS/MND to City Council. The subject property is 13310 Rosecrans
  Avenue, located on the southwest corner of Rosecrans Avenue and Marilla Avenue.
  That the Planning Commission:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-22 to recommend approval to City Council for General Plan Amendment No.
  2022-03 subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 23-23 to recommend approval to City Council for Zone Change No. 2022-05
  subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  3. Adopt Resolution No. 23-24 approving Tentative Parcel Map No. 2022-04 subject to the Conditions of
  Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  4. Review and recommend adoption to City Council of the associated IS/MND.

4.  Tentative Parcel Map No. 2022-01 to permit the subdivision of an existing parcel into two (2) parcels.
  Environmental: Consider and find the project exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15315 (Minor Land
  Divisions). The subject property is 11301 Firestone Boulevard, located on the northwest corner of
  Firestone Boulevard and Orr and Day Road.
  That the Planning Commission:

Planning Commission, September 13, 2023  Page 2 of 3
   1. Adopt Resolution No. 23-25 approving Tentative Parcel Map No. 2022-01 subject to the Conditions of
  Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  2. Consider and find that the project is exempt from California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15315 (Minor Land Divisions).

REPORTS

5.  ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES PLAN UPDATE DISCUSSION
  Staff recommends that the Planning Commission receive and file.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I, John P. Ramirez, AICP, Director of Community Development/Secretary, hereby certify that the foregoing
agenda was posted at City Hall not less than 72-hours before the start of the meeting and forwarded to each
member of the Norwalk Planning Commission and to the following newspapers: Herald American, Los Cerritos
Community News, Norwalk Patriot, and Whittier Daily News, all on September 8, 2023.

John P. Ramirez, AICP
Planning Commission Secretary

Planning Commission, September 13, 2023  Page 3 of 3
